```{r}
#setwd("C:/Users/Emily Haak/OneDrive/OneDrive - The Pennsylvania State University/STAT 462")

movie <- read.csv("movie_blockbusters.csv")
head(movie)
attach(movie)

nrow(movie)
#Dataset includes 5000 movies 

summary(movie)

cor(movie[,c(6,7,8,9,11,13)])

# revenue and profit have the highest correlation of 0.9843939494

table(movie$blockbuster)
#673 blockbusters and 4327 non-blockbusters


#Counting the zeros in each column to see if there are unmeaningful zeros
colSums(movie == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
#with the variables we are looking at there are no unmeaningful zeros

colSums(is.na(movie))
#checking if missing values in dataset - none 
```

```{r}
hist(movie$profit_usd)
#cannot take log of negative numbers so this 

```

```{r}
#Fitting first regression model
movie_model1 <- lm(blockbuster~ rating + budget_usd + revenue_usd + runtime_min + profit_usd + popularity)
summary(movie_model1)

#Looking at genre by itself
genre_model = lm(blockbuster~ genre)
summary(genre_model)

#Fitting model w/ log transformations
movie_model2 <- lm(blockbuster~ rating + log(budget_usd) + log(revenue_usd) + runtime_min + profit_usd + log(popularity))
summary(movie_model2)

# Histogram 
hist(movie_model2$residuals)

# QQ-plot
qqnorm(movie_model2$residuals)
qqline(movie_model2$residuals)

# Shapiro test
shapiro.test(movie_model2$residuals) 



```

```{r}
# budget by blockbuster status
boxplot(budget_usd ~ blockbuster, data = movie,
        names = c("Not blockbuster", "Blockbuster"),
        xlab = "Movie status",
        ylab = "Budget (USD)",
        main = "Budget by Blockbuster Status",
        log = "y") # need log transformation
```
